 'A different test to what we've faced this season' published at 19:59 BST 19:59 BST 
 Ipswich v Nottm Forest (20:00 BST) 
 Ipswich Town 
 Ipswich boss Gary O'Neil speaking to Sky Sports about the switch to a back four: "The team today allows us to get more attacking players on the pitch. I don't think we'll always look like a back four tonight, at times we'll look like a back five. We want as many attacking players on the pitch as we can."
 On dealing with Nottingham Forest's transitions and how they do that: "Lots of things. We need to be really secure with the ball. If you lose the ball in central, dangerous areas they will get to the goal really quickly and then how well we deal with it because we are going to lose the ball at times. That will be a test, as will be their direct play. They are a very direct side so their set-pieces will be key too. 
 "It is going to be a big test for us. It will be a different test probably to what we've faced so far so we'll learn about ourselves again today and hopefully one we can come out on top in."
 27 3 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 19:57 BST 19:57 BST 
 Ipswich v Nottm Forest (20:00 BST) 
 Image source, Getty Images Last week Ipswich probably thought themselves unlucky to come away from the Etihad empty handed after they gave Enzo Maresca's Manchester City a real run for it in a 3-2 defeat.
 But Gary O'Neil praised his side's togetherness, resilience and ability to adapt as they continue to improve in the Premier League.
 Their three wins place them 10th in the table.
 46 5 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Forest are a win away from being on a roll' published at 19:56 BST 19:56 BST 
 Ipswich v Nottm Forest (20:00 BST) 
 Don Hutchison 
Former Premier League midfielder on 5 Live 
 Looking at the team tonight, it is a strong 11 for Forest. The bench isn't that strong and the depth isn't there, so he could do with a few more bodies but I can see Glasner's methods. 
 Forest are a win away from being on a roll.
